paragraphs.source_en: “There are more things I would like to show you. Please ask the senior retainers to come over here as well.” The monk Tenku called the senior retainers to Jirosaburo’s side, then displayed before them, one by one, the objects that the Matsudaira clan had donated to Daijuji Temple over the years. The offerings made by Hirotada, who had died at only twenty-four, were especially numerous, filling Jirosaburo’s heart with sorrow. There was a portrait of Prince Shotoku, a hanging scroll by Muqi, and waka poems written in Hirotada’s own hand.
